roadmap.title: Foundations and bounded runtime
roadmap.question: What is an agent, and how does Cogentrex keep execution bounded?
roadmap.outcome: Explain the trust boundary, typed contracts, state machine, and ReAct loop.

roadmap.title: Tools and governance
roadmap.question: How can a model request effects without receiving unchecked power?
roadmap.outcome: Trace a tool call through schema validation, policy, approval, isolation, and idempotency.

roadmap.title: Context, memory, and grounded knowledge
roadmap.question: What information enters a run, persists between runs, or supports an answer?
roadmap.outcome: Distinguish context, durable memory, retrieval, grounding, citations, and faithfulness.

roadmap.title: Evaluation and resilience
roadmap.question: How does Cogentrex measure quality and respond to failure?
roadmap.outcome: Explain recorded evaluation, drift, retries, breakers, fallbacks, rate limits, and jobs.

roadmap.title: Delegation and governed integrations
roadmap.question: How does work cross agent and process boundaries safely?
roadmap.outcome: Explain bounded delegation, lineage, signed envelopes, governed stdio MCP profiles, scoped inventory, and why Streamable HTTP remains unimplemented.

roadmap.title: Product surface and operations
roadmap.question: How does the user inspect Cogentrex, and how is the local system operated?
roadmap.outcome: Demonstrate auth, SSE, observability, multimodal artifacts, Docker, migrations, backup, and readiness.

modules.title: 00 — Agent anatomy
modules.summary: By the end you can name an agent's boundaries, trace startup and one request, and separate control logic from model behavior. Prerequisites: basic Python functions, HTTP, and the terms model , tool , policy , event , and adapter . Start with Agent anatomy.
modules.mental_model: A chatbot maps text to text. An agent may ask a model what to do, invoke effects, feed observations back, and stop. Therefore the model is an untrusted planner inside a deterministic control plane—not the application. Cogentrex is a custom typed runtime ; it does not use an agent framework.

modules.title: 01 — Python architecture: OOP, Protocols, DI, and async
modules.summary: You will read Cogentrex's Python boundaries, explain application composition, structural typing and dependency injection (DI), and identify where async work can block or be cancelled. Prerequisites: classes, type hints, await , and context managers. Canonical reading: Application factory, middleware, routers, and application state, OOP, Protocols, and DI, and Async Python.
modules.mental_model: The application factory owns process composition: it seeds application state, registers the middleware onion and router groups, and separates liveness from readiness. The runtime should depend on capabilities, not vendors or databases. Frozen dataclasses carry values; Protocols define ports; concrete adapters are injected at application/request composition roots.

modules.title: 02 — Typed runtime and state machine
modules.summary: You will trace immutable messages and native tool calls, model runtime transitions, and interpret every terminal StopReason . Prerequisites: Modules 00–01 and Python dataclasses/enums. Read Typed runtime and State machines, then use the runtime walkthrough.
modules.mental_model: AgentRuntime.run is an explicit bounded state machine even though it is implemented as a loop rather than a state-machine library. Typed values prevent text scraping from becoming an execution protocol.

modules.title: 03 — ReAct loop, budgets, and stop reasons
modules.summary: You will distinguish reasoning/action/observation iteration from reflection, verifier delegation, and post-run evaluation; then test a bounded recovery path. Prerequisites: Module 02. Read ReAct, State machines, and Idempotency.
modules.mental_model: ReAct alternates model decisions and tool observations. Cogentrex does not expose hidden chain-of-thought; it handles provider-native calls and visible observations. A tool error can be returned to the model for another bounded attempt. That is local error feedback—not final-answer reflection. Separately, optional BoundedReflectionService can critique a completed unstructured draft without tools and perform at most one hard-bounded revision. The evidence-only verifier child and recorded-run evaluations are also…

modules.title: 04 — Tool contracts and schemas
modules.summary: You will register a typed tool, explain validation order, and test malformed arguments without executing a handler. Prerequisites: Modules 01–03 and JSON objects. Read Tool contracts, JSON Schema, and the tool registry walkthrough.
modules.mental_model: A tool is an effectful capability behind metadata and gates—not an arbitrary Python function offered directly to a model. Registration validates trusted metadata; execution validates untrusted arguments, permissions, timeout, and audit behavior.

modules.title: 05 — Policy and durable approvals
modules.summary: You will predict ALLOW/ASK/DENY, explain exact-bound durable approval, and test atomic one-shot decisions. Prerequisites: Modules 02–04, hashes, and database transactions. Read Policy engine, Durable approvals, Idempotency, and the policy/approval walkthrough.
modules.mental_model: Policy answers whether a classified request may proceed. Approval supplies a human decision only for ASK ; it does not replace policy. A receipt binds owner, conversation, run, native call ID, canonical tool name, and canonical argument hash so approval cannot be replayed for changed work.

modules.title: Module 06 — Context, conversations, and encrypted memory
modules.summary: A model does not remember a chat by itself. Cogentrex constructs each request from a system instruction, tool descriptions, selected persistent facts, recent conversation messages, and the new user turn. Context is the bounded input sent now; conversation history is durable message data; memory is selected durable facts. Treating these as separate stores prevents accidental cross-user recall and makes deletion and provenance comprehensible.
modules.mental_model: Think of a packing list, not a brain: the database owns history and facts; build messages chooses what enters this model call. Facts are an encrypted, quota-bounded notebook keyed by (user id, project id) . A checkpoint freezes state for restoration/forking; it is not automatically replayed model execution.

modules.title: Module 07 — Durable Run Ledger, replay, fork, and compare
modules.summary: A chat answer alone cannot explain what an agent did. The Run Ledger stores an ordered, owner-scoped trajectory: policy decisions, tool metadata, evidence IDs, token totals, stop reason, lineage, and bounded display metadata. Replay reads stored facts; fork copies safe conversation state at an event boundary; compare places two stored trajectories side by side. None reruns a model or tool.
modules.mental_model: The ledger is a flight recorder. RunRow is the flight summary; RuntimeEventRow records ordered instrument readings. It deliberately stores hashes, IDs, counts, and decisions rather than prompts, chain-of-thought, tool arguments, or results.

modules.title: Module 08 — Documents, embeddings, RAG, and grounded answers
modules.summary: RAG retrieves document chunks before asking a model to answer. An embedding maps text to numbers; retrieval ranks chunks by similarity; generation writes claims from those chunks; verification decides whether each claim has conservative support; citations point back to evidence. A similar chunk is not proof that an answer is true.
modules.mental_model: Retrieval is a librarian, generation is a writer, verification is a fact checker, and citations are shelf labels. One role cannot substitute for another.

modules.title: Module 09 — Evaluation harness and regression evidence
modules.summary: An evaluation turns examples and expectations into repeatable measurements. Cogentrex has a lightweight live-call EvalHarness , heuristic evaluators, and a stronger durable path that evaluates already-completed Run Ledger trajectories against a versioned, hash-verified dataset. The durable path does not call a model, retriever, or tool.
modules.mental_model: A test harness is a ruler. A versioned dataset says what is measured; an evaluator defines marks on the ruler; persistence makes results auditable; a threshold is a policy decision. A precise ruler can consistently measure the wrong thing, so validity must be argued separately from reproducibility.

modules.title: Module 10 — Resilience: idempotency, retries, deadlines, breakers, fallback, and rate limits
modules.summary: Failures are normal: providers time out, clients disconnect, retries duplicate work, and traffic spikes. Resilience means bounding damage and preserving a truthful terminal state—not merely “trying again.” Cogentrex demonstrates idempotent creation/finalization guards, bounded retries in selected paths, timeout/cancellation handling, a concurrency-safe circuit breaker, fallback adapters, and sliding-window rate limiting.
modules.mental_model: Use layered bulkheads: idempotency prevents duplicate state; deadlines bound time; cancellation stops unwanted work and finalizes evidence; retries handle classified transient failures within a budget; a breaker stops hammering an unhealthy dependency; fallback changes the service path; rate limiting controls admission. Each layer has different semantics.

modules.title: Module 11 — Bounded delegation and hybrid orchestration
modules.summary: Cogentrex has two distinct bounded delegation paths. The verifier sees a sealed claim/evidence packet and has no tools. The hybrid pilot can run a fixed researcher and a server-templated dynamic analyst with read-only capability subsets. Both paths use finite budgets, signed one-use scope, durable lineage, and fail-closed validation; model output can still be wrong.
modules.mental_model: Use a sealed review packet. The parent supplies exact claims and evidence IDs; the child cannot fetch more evidence or use tools. The model output is untrusted until strict parsing proves every claim appears exactly once and every cited evidence ID was delegated. The invariant is bounded authority, not model infallibility.

modules.title: Module 12 — Governed MCP discovery and execution
modules.summary: MCP standardizes tool discovery and calls; it does not confer trust. Cogentrex supports one concrete path: deployment-owned stdio profiles become scoped inventory, then immutable runtime bindings that still cross schema, policy, approval and timeout controls.
modules.mental_model: Think “controlled adapter pipeline,” not “install any plugin.” Operators own executable profiles; users select only safe profile IDs. Discovery imports bounded metadata. The runtime exposes enabled healthy tools only, revalidates the binding immediately before transport use, then sends it through SecureToolRegistry. The connection to the course spine is explicit: Policy → Run → Approval → Tool → Evidence → Evaluation . Inputs are authenticated/scoped data; outputs are typed results plus inspectable evidence;…

modules.title: Module 13 — Authentication, ownership, SSE, UI, and observability
modules.summary: One request crosses several different boundaries: credentials establish identity, owner/project scopes data, policy governs actions, SSE projects progress, and observability emits safe operational signals. None substitutes for another. SSE is transient; durable run and evaluation records have separate persistence contracts.
modules.mental_model: Identity is the root label, owner/project is the data fence, policy is the action gate, and observability is the instrument panel. SSE is only a projection of typed events; the Run Ledger remains durable evidence. Logs describe, metrics aggregate, and traces time the path—none alone proves semantic correctness. The connection to the course spine is explicit: Policy → Run → Approval → Tool → Evidence → Evaluation . Inputs are authenticated/scoped data; outputs are typed results plus inspectable evidence; mutable…

modules.title: Module 14 — Local operations: Compose, health, migrations, CI, and recovery
modules.summary: Operations asks whether a specific build can start, become ready, preserve schema, pass clean-worker gates, and recover durable state. Compose files and scripts are recipes; only revision- and environment-scoped executions are observations.
modules.mental_model: Operations is a chain of evidence: configuration → start → migrate → ready → serve → observe → back up → destroy → restore → verify exact records. A manifest is a recipe, not proof the meal was cooked. A backup is unproven until restored. The connection to the course spine is explicit: Policy → Run → Approval → Tool → Evidence → Evaluation . Inputs are authenticated/scoped data; outputs are typed results plus inspectable evidence; mutable authority never comes from model prose.

modules.title: Module 15 — Capstone: evidence-first demo and interview defense
modules.summary: The capstone is claim control: say exactly what exists, how it is wired, what tests establish, what was observed, and what remains unverified. A persuasive demo does not merge distinct proof paths or turn local evidence into production claims.
modules.mental_model: Build the story as a proof graph. Every claim points to source, test, observed artifact, and limitation. The graph may stop at local observation; never draw an unsupported edge to production. The demo spine is Policy → Run → Approval → Tool → Evidence → Evaluation, with auth/ownership around it and operations beneath it. The connection to the course spine is explicit: Policy → Run → Approval → Tool → Evidence → Evaluation . Inputs are authenticated/scoped data; outputs are typed results plus inspectable evidence;…

concepts.title: Agent anatomy and trust boundaries
concepts.module_title: 00 — Agent anatomy
concepts.summary: An agent is a program that lets a language model propose the next step, including a typed tool call, while ordinary code decides what is permitted and when the run must stop. A chatbot can return text only; an agent may affect files, networks, or databases, so its control plane matters as much as its prompt. In Cogentrex, the model is an untrusted planner. The custom runtime—not a framework such as LangChain or LangGraph—owns authority, execution, budgets, and evidence.
concepts.mental_model: Treat the system as a guarded interpreter: the model emits proposals; the runtime interprets only native, typed proposals that pass every guard. The key invariant is proposal is not permission . A convincing model response cannot call a handler directly.
concepts.limitations: Custom local runtime; no agent framework and no public production evidence.

concepts.title: Application factory, middleware, routers, and application state
concepts.module_title: 01 — Python architecture: OOP, Protocols, DI, and async
concepts.summary: Before FastAPI can receive a useful request, the application must be assembled. Cogentrex centralizes that assembly in create app() . A factory is a function responsible for constructing and configuring another object. create app() returns one consistently wired FastAPI application. Production calls it with default collaborators; tests may inject controlled settings or replacement constructors. Middleware forms an onion around each endpoint. A request travels inward through the registered layers, the endpoint…
concepts.mental_model: Without one composition boundary, route modules could construct their own providers, repositories, security components, and clients. That creates inconsistent configuration, duplicated resources, hidden ownership, and tests that require real infrastructure. Use this mental model: The factory controls assembly order. Lifespan controls the live resources' start and stop. Routes consume those resources; they do not own them.
concepts.limitations: Application composition and local probe contracts are implemented; readiness is point-in-time and does not actively call every reported capability or prove public availability.

concepts.title: Python OOP, Protocols, and dependency injection
concepts.module_title: 01 — Python architecture: OOP, Protocols, DI, and async
concepts.summary: Object-oriented design groups behavior with the state and invariants it owns. A Python Protocol states which methods a collaborator must provide without requiring inheritance. Dependency injection (DI) supplies collaborators from outside, making control flow explicit and allowing small test doubles.
concepts.mental_model: Core runtime logic should say “complete these typed messages” rather than “call this vendor SDK and read its global configuration.” Protocols form sockets; adapters are plugs; the composition root chooses which valid plug powers each socket.
concepts.limitations: Protocols and mocks prove interfaces, not external-adapter behavior.

concepts.title: Async Python and cancellation
concepts.module_title: 01 — Python architecture: OOP, Protocols, DI, and async
concepts.summary: async def creates a coroutine: work that can pause at await so the event loop can run other ready work. This is especially useful for model, database, approval, and network waits. Async concurrency does not make CPU-heavy Python execute in parallel, and cancellation does not roll back effects that already escaped the process.
concepts.mental_model: Picture one cashier who starts several remote orders and serves whoever is ready rather than staring at one oven. Between two lines with no await , coroutine code is synchronous; at every await , assume shared state or collaborator-owned data may change.
concepts.limitations: Cancellation and timeout cannot roll back a committed external effect.

concepts.title: Typed provider-neutral runtime
concepts.module_title: 02 — Typed runtime and state machine
concepts.summary: A typed runtime represents messages, model responses, tool calls, usage, events, budgets, and outcomes as named validated values instead of loosely related dictionaries and magic strings. Types make illegal states harder to construct and responsibilities easier to inspect. Cogentrex implements a custom typed runtime ; it is not LangChain, LangGraph, or another agent framework.
concepts.mental_model: A runtime is a protocol between components. If “tool call,” “assistant response,” and “stop” are only conventions inside dictionaries, misspellings and missing fields become late production failures. Typed values are labeled shipping containers; validation checks the seal, while snapshots ensure another party cannot swap contents after inspection.
concepts.limitations: External provider token accuracy and production load are unverified.

concepts.title: Runtime state machine and stop reasons
concepts.module_title: 02 — Typed runtime and state machine
concepts.summary: A state machine names possible states, the events that move between them, guards that allow transitions, and terminal outcomes. Code need not use a state-machine library to have state-machine semantics. Making the model explicit exposes impossible transitions, races, and missing cleanup paths.
concepts.mental_model: Ask four questions at every step: where are we, what input is legal, what invariant must hold, and how can we stop? Cogentrex's runtime, approval, and run-ledger lifecycles overlap, but they are distinct machines: a pending approval is not itself a runtime stop reason or ledger status.
concepts.limitations: Implemented as explicit loop control, not a state-machine framework.

concepts.title: Bounded ReAct-style tool loop
concepts.module_title: 03 — ReAct loop, budgets, and stop reasons
concepts.summary: ReAct is an iterative action/observation pattern: the model proposes a tool action, controlled code executes it, and the resulting observation informs the model's next response. Cogentrex uses provider-native ToolCall values rather than parsing actions from model prose. It does not expose or require private chain-of-thought; observable progress, calls, results, and final answers are enough to run the loop. One configured tool-call allowance is shown to the model and enforced by the runtime; when the boundary is…
concepts.mental_model: Models cannot directly know fresh external state. The loop turns tools into controlled sensors/actuators and lets observations update the next proposal. The runtime is a referee: it limits rounds, blocks repeated plays, authorizes actions, and decides when the game ends.
concepts.limitations: Tool-error feedback is not generic self-reflection.

concepts.title: Generic critique and revision self-reflection
concepts.module_title: 03 — ReAct loop, budgets, and stop reasons
concepts.summary: Self-reflection is a second, deliberately bounded look at a proposed final answer. Cogentrex first produces the normal draft. If reflection is enabled, a tool-free critic returns a small structured verdict: keep or revise, issue codes, validated request:L / draft:L evidence locations, and confidence. A revise verdict permits at most one tool-free revision. This is different from ReAct tool-error feedback, verifier delegation, and post-run scoring.
concepts.mental_model: ReAct alternates model decisions and tool observations. Cogentrex does not expose hidden chain-of-thought; it handles provider-native calls and visible observations. A tool error can be returned to the model for another bounded attempt. That is local error feedback—not final-answer reflection. Separately, optional BoundedReflectionService can critique a completed unstructured draft without tools and perform at most one hard-bounded revision. The evidence-only verifier child and recorded-run evaluations are also…
concepts.limitations: Bounded local final-answer reflection is implemented; the recorded synthetic fixture does not prove live-provider benefit or generalization, and no learned reflection memory exists.

concepts.title: Secure typed tool contracts
concepts.module_title: 04 — Tool contracts and schemas
concepts.summary: A tool contract turns an application capability into a bounded interface a model can propose using. It includes more than a function name: input shape, handler, timeout, permissions, risk classes, resource identity, and an approval hint. The model sees a reduced provider definition; trusted control-plane metadata stays server-side.
concepts.mental_model: A tool contract is both an API boundary and a capability boundary. Keep the menu shown to the model separate from the kitchen's safety rules: descriptions help selection, while trusted metadata controls execution.
concepts.limitations: Handler semantics and effect rollback remain adapter responsibilities.

concepts.title: Tool input JSON Schema subset
concepts.module_title: 04 — Tool contracts and schemas
concepts.summary: JSON Schema is a vocabulary for describing the shape of JSON data. Cogentrex uses a deliberately small, custom-validated subset to reject malformed tool arguments before permissions or handler code run. It is an intentionally bounded contract—not a claim of compliance with the full JSON Schema specification.
concepts.mental_model: A schema is a syntactic gate between probabilistic output and deterministic code. Think of it as an airport document check: it rejects the wrong shape, but it does not establish permission, benign intent, or safe destination.
concepts.limitations: The documented object/property/type/enum validation subset is fail-closed, rejects unknown schema keywords, and is tested; recursive or remote full-spec JSON Schema is intentionally outside this tool-contract boundary.

concepts.title: Deterministic policy engine
concepts.module_title: 05 — Policy and durable approvals
concepts.summary: A policy engine answers a narrow question: given a canonical tool, concrete resources, and declared risks, should the runtime ALLOW , ASK , or DENY ? It is deterministic code, not an LLM judgment. It neither executes the tool nor collects the human response; those are separate responsibilities.
concepts.mental_model: Keep proposal, classification, human consent, and execution as separate gates. Policy is a pure decision table over trusted canonical facts; the runtime enforces its answer and verifies that the facts cannot change before dispatch.
concepts.limitations: Path policy matching is lexical; execution must enforce containment.

concepts.title: Exact-bound durable approvals
concepts.module_title: 05 — Policy and durable approvals
concepts.summary: A durable approval is a database-backed, expiring decision about one exact proposed effect. It is not “this user trusts the terminal tool”; it is “this owner approves this call ID, canonical tool name, and argument digest in this run before expiry.” Persistence lets a different process or a restarted waiter observe the decision without broadening permission.
concepts.mental_model: Human latency is much longer than a request handler's normal lifetime. Model approval as a one-use ticket in durable storage, not as a Boolean future tied to one process. The ticket permits only the effect whose identity was shown; changing the arguments invalidates the ticket.
concepts.limitations: Locally verified; no multi-region consistency or public SLO claim.

concepts.title: Idempotency and exactly-once claim boundaries
concepts.module_title: 05 — Policy and durable approvals
concepts.summary: An operation is idempotent when repeating the same logical request does not create extra effects after the first successful application. “Set status to approved” can be idempotent; “send another email” usually is not unless the receiver recognizes a stable operation key. Retries are safe only when every effect they may repeat has a duplicate-detection or reconciliation rule.
concepts.mental_model: A client can time out after the server committed but before receiving the response. The retry is ambiguous: did the first attempt fail, or did only its acknowledgement fail? Place stable identity and atomic deduplication at the effect , not merely at the HTTP endpoint.
concepts.limitations: Durable HMAC-bound first-writer-wins effect reservations are proven under PostgreSQL contention; universal exactly-once behavior in arbitrary external systems is explicitly not claimed.

concepts.title: Context windows
concepts.module_title: Module 06 — Context, conversations, and encrypted memory
concepts.summary: A context window is everything sent to the model for one invocation. It can include system instructions, tool descriptions, selected durable facts, recent conversation messages, images, and the current user turn. The window is temporary: it is constructed for a request and is not itself a durable memory store. A model can only condition its answer on content that fits and is selected, even if much more data exists in the database. Three layers must stay distinct: 1. Conversation rows are durable ordered…
concepts.mental_model: Think of a packing list, not a brain: the database owns history and facts; build messages chooses what enters this model call. Facts are an encrypted, quota-bounded notebook keyed by (user id, project id) . A checkpoint freezes state for restoration/forking; it is not automatically replayed model execution.
concepts.limitations: The fail-closed bound covers roles/content, image refs, tool_call_id, tool-call JSON, tool definitions, response format and response-contract schema; images are revalidated and reserve 22k tokens each. It is deliberately conservative rather than provider-exact, and provenance remains initial-context rather than per-call.

concepts.title: Conversation lifecycle
concepts.module_title: Module 06 — Context, conversations, and encrypted memory
concepts.summary: A conversation is the durable chat container a user sees: metadata plus ordered user and assistant messages. A run is one execution attempt associated with a conversation. One conversation can accumulate many turns and many runs over time. When a new model call starts, Cogentrex selects some conversation rows into an effective context, but the conversation itself remains larger and durable. Keep these stores separate: Object Persists Scope Purpose --- --- --- --- ConversationRow ID, title, owner, timestamps,…
concepts.mental_model: Think of a packing list, not a brain: the database owns history and facts; build messages chooses what enters this model call. Facts are an encrypted, quota-bounded notebook keyed by (user id, project id) . A checkpoint freezes state for restoration/forking; it is not automatically replayed model execution.
concepts.limitations: Conversation rows are redacted persistent history, distinct from encrypted fact memory; automatic expiry is absent.

concepts.title: Encrypted memory
concepts.module_title: Module 06 — Context, conversations, and encrypted memory
concepts.summary: Encrypted memory is Cogentrex's durable store for selected facts such as a user preference. Before a fact is written, Cogentrex redacts it, packages content with provenance, derives a scope-specific key, and encrypts the package with authenticated encryption. On read, it verifies authenticity before returning plaintext to the authorized application path. Encryption protects database bytes at rest from casual disclosure. Authorization decides who may request decryption. Redaction reduces sensitive content before…
concepts.mental_model: Think of a packing list, not a brain: the database owns history and facts; build messages chooses what enters this model call. Facts are an encrypted, quota-bounded notebook keyed by (user id, project id) . A checkpoint freezes state for restoration/forking; it is not automatically replayed model execution.
concepts.limitations: No online key rotation, automatic expiry, external KMS, or production security certification.

concepts.title: Checkpoints
concepts.module_title: Module 06 — Context, conversations, and encrypted memory
concepts.summary: A checkpoint names a stable boundary and saves the state that Cogentrex explicitly knows how to persist at that boundary. Think of it as a photograph of selected application data, not a virtual-machine image. Cogentrex has two different implementations: a small in-memory teaching utility and the durable checkpoint created by the Run Ledger fork path. The durable path copies redacted conversation rows through a selected run-event time and records lineage metadata. It does not turn time backward, undo an email,…
concepts.mental_model: Think of a packing list, not a brain: the database owns history and facts; build messages chooses what enters this model call. Facts are an encrypted, quota-bounded notebook keyed by (user id, project id) . A checkpoint freezes state for restoration/forking; it is not automatically replayed model execution.
concepts.limitations: Cogentrex checkpoints restore durable safe conversation/run state for replay and fork; arbitrary filesystem workspace, process, tool, and external-side-effect restoration is explicitly outside this server-product boundary.

concepts.title: Durable Run Ledger
concepts.module_title: Module 07 — Durable Run Ledger, replay, fork, and compare
concepts.summary: A Run Ledger answers operational questions about one agent execution: when it began, which safe control events committed, whether policy or approval intervened, how it ended, and what bounded metrics were recorded. Each run has one summary row and an ordered sequence of event rows. The sequence is append-only while the run is active and frozen after terminal completion. “Flight recorder” does not mean “record everything.” Cogentrex deliberately excludes raw prompts, hidden reasoning, tool arguments/results,…
concepts.mental_model: The ledger is a flight recorder. RunRow is the flight summary; RuntimeEventRow records ordered instrument readings. It deliberately stores hashes, IDs, counts, and decisions rather than prompts, chain-of-thought, tool arguments, or results.
concepts.limitations: Recorded events are evidence of control flow, not semantic truth or tamper-proof WORM audit storage.

concepts.title: Replay, fork, and compare
concepts.module_title: Module 07 — Durable Run Ledger, replay, fork, and compare
concepts.summary: These three operations answer different questions: - Replay: “What safe events were recorded for this run, in order?” - Fork: “Create a new conversation branch from the stored state at this event boundary.” - Compare: “How do two stored run summaries and trajectories differ?” Replay is not rerun. It makes no model or tool call and therefore cannot reproduce nondeterministic output or side effects. Fork is not rewind. It does not undo the source or reconstruct process memory, open files, credentials, network…
concepts.mental_model: The ledger is a flight recorder. RunRow is the flight summary; RuntimeEventRow records ordered instrument readings. It deliberately stores hashes, IDs, counts, and decisions rather than prompts, chain-of-thought, tool arguments, or results.
concepts.limitations: Replay and compare are stored-only; fork does not rerun tools or restore arbitrary external workspace state.

concepts.title: Document chunking
concepts.module_title: Module 08 — Documents, embeddings, RAG, and grounded answers
concepts.summary: RAG retrieves document chunks before asking a model to answer. An embedding maps text to numbers; retrieval ranks chunks by similarity; generation writes claims from those chunks; verification decides whether each claim has conservative support; citations point back to evidence. A similar chunk is not proof that an answer is true.
concepts.mental_model: Think of a document as a map and chunks as map tiles. Tiny tiles are precise but may omit landmarks needed for orientation. Huge tiles preserve context but make every match broad and expensive. Overlap is the strip printed on two adjacent tiles; it helps continuity but does not create new information.
concepts.limitations: Character-based defaults are not corpus-optimized and do not preserve rich document structures.

concepts.title: Embeddings
concepts.module_title: Module 08 — Documents, embeddings, RAG, and grounded answers
concepts.summary: RAG retrieves document chunks before asking a model to answer. An embedding maps text to numbers; retrieval ranks chunks by similarity; generation writes claims from those chunks; verification decides whether each claim has conservative support; citations point back to evidence. A similar chunk is not proof that an answer is true.
concepts.mental_model: Imagine a coordinate map where semantically related passages should appear near one another. The map is learned, not a database of facts. Changing the embedding model is like changing coordinate systems: old and new coordinates should not be mixed. A compass can point toward a likely neighborhood without proving that a particular house contains the answer.
concepts.limitations: Azure Foundry text-embedding-3-small is live-proven for vector generation and ingest/query retrieval in a development deployment; broad domain retrieval and production SLA are not claimed.

concepts.title: Scoped SQL JSON cosine retrieval
concepts.module_title: Module 08 — Documents, embeddings, RAG, and grounded answers
concepts.summary: RAG retrieves document chunks before asking a model to answer. An embedding maps text to numbers; retrieval ranks chunks by similarity; generation writes claims from those chunks; verification decides whether each claim has conservative support; citations point back to evidence. A similar chunk is not proof that an answer is true.
concepts.mental_model: Retrieval is a librarian selecting a short stack before a researcher writes an answer. A well-chosen stack improves the opportunity to answer. The researcher can still misread it, invent details, or answer the wrong question. Authorization determines which shelves the librarian may inspect before ranking begins.
concepts.limitations: JSON vectors are scanned and cosine-ranked in Python; this is not pgvector or indexed production vector serving.

concepts.title: Retrieval-augmented generation
concepts.module_title: Module 08 — Documents, embeddings, RAG, and grounded answers
concepts.summary: RAG retrieves document chunks before asking a model to answer. An embedding maps text to numbers; retrieval ranks chunks by similarity; generation writes claims from those chunks; verification decides whether each claim has conservative support; citations point back to evidence. It does not use binary floating point in authoritative counters. The reservation is sized from the current serialized request plus bounded headroom and the maximum eligible…
concepts.mental_model: The ledger is a flight recorder. RunRow is the flight summary; RuntimeEventRow records ordered instrument readings. It deliberately stores hashes, IDs, counts, and decisions rather than prompts, chain-of-thought, tool arguments, or results.
concepts.limitations: Atomic run/project reservation and reconciliation are live-proven for chat, RAG and verifier calls; price-book versioning, period policies, operator resolution of indeterminate charges and budget-management UI remain future work.

concepts.title: Structured output and prompt caching
concepts.module_title: 02 — Typed runtime and state machine
concepts.summary: Structured output is a contract: the model response must parse as strict JSON and satisfy an application validator before Cogentrex treats it as a successful answer. A provider's JSON hint or native schema improves generation but does not replace local validation. Prompt caching is separately observable accounting. A cache marker merely requests reuse; only provider-reported cache-read or cache-write counters prove what the provider reported for that call. Local tests prove normalization and arithmetic, not a…
concepts.mental_model: Keep these layers distinct: 1. Requested format: JSON mode or provider-native JSON Schema. 2. Transport response: provider text, tool calls, usage, and stop reason. 3. Local trust boundary: strict JSON parse and application validation. 4. Cache request: an eligible stable prompt prefix is marked. 5. Cache evidence: provider-reported counters are normalized and priced per response. A response is not trusted merely because the provider says it used a schema. Cache savings are not inferred from a request marker.
concepts.limitations: Foundry JSON prompting is followed by strict local Draft 2020-12 validation and one bounded retry; native provider-side JSON Schema is not claimed. Cache controls and counters are wired, but the live probe observed zero cache tokens and makes no savings claim.

concepts.title: Multimodal input and artifacts
concepts.module_title: Module 13 — Authentication, ownership, SSE, UI, and observability
concepts.summary: An image string is not trusted merely because it starts with data:image . Cogentrex caps the encoded request, decodes strict base64, inspects actual image bytes, compares the declared MIME type, rejects oversized dimensions before pixel decoding, strips metadata by re-encoding pixels, and caps the sanitized output. Only then may the image enter a model request. Artifacts are a separate output concern. This note focuses on provider-bound image inputs; existing artifact ownership and inert-rendering controls remain…
concepts.mental_model: Identity is the root label, owner/project is the data fence, policy is the action gate, and observability is the instrument panel. SSE is only a projection of typed events; the Run Ledger remains durable evidence. Logs describe, metrics aggregate, and traces time the path—none alone proves semantic correctness. The connection to the course spine is explicit: Policy → Run → Approval → Tool → Evidence → Evaluation . Inputs are authenticated/scoped data; outputs are typed results plus inspectable evidence; mutable…
concepts.limitations: Authenticated sync and SSE paths validate and sanitize bounded image inputs before persistence/provider execution, and deterministic tests prove OpenAI, Anthropic, and Ollama request construction. No external vision-provider observation, malware scanner, durable attachment backend, or public deployment is claimed.

concepts.title: Background jobs and scheduling
concepts.module_title: Module 10 — Resilience: idempotency, retries, deadlines, breakers, fallback, and rate limits
concepts.summary: A background job continues after the HTTP request that created it. A reliable queue must persist the job, let only one worker claim a particular lease, recover abandoned work, limit retries, and prevent stale workers from committing results. asyncio.create task() alone is not a durable queue: process restart loses both work and status.
concepts.mental_model: Use layered bulkheads: idempotency prevents duplicate state; deadlines bound time; cancellation stops unwanted work and finalizes evidence; retries handle classified transient failures within a budget; a breaker stops hammering an unhealthy dependency; fallback changes the service path; rate limiting controls admission. Each layer has different semantics.
concepts.limitations: Durable owner/project-scoped SQL jobs have atomic claims, monotonic lease fencing, heartbeat, retry/dead-letter, cancellation, restart persistence and UI. Execution is at-least-once, not exactly-once. In-process cancellation-resistant coroutines cannot be forcibly killed, so non-idempotent external-effect job kinds are prohibited; process isolation is deferred to S8.7.

concepts.title: Compliance controls and red teaming
concepts.module_title: Module 09 — Evaluation harness and regression evidence
concepts.summary: Compliance controls encode obligations such as prohibited content or required disclaimers. Red teaming deliberately probes bypasses and unsafe behavior. A list of blocked phrases is a test aid, not legal certification, and testing a guardrail in isolation is not testing the whole agent.
concepts.mental_model: Treat the boundary as a contract with explicit inputs, outputs, state, failure behavior, and evidence. The important question is not whether a similarly named class or file exists, but whether the behavior is wired into a real path and whether a test or observation proves it.
concepts.limitations: Mandatory deterministic compliance runs before supported chat, document, structured-output and effect boundaries, with admin-only guardrail/fuzz tests. This is a local technical baseline, not legal certification or an exhaustive external red-team program.

concepts.title: Agent communication security
concepts.module_title: Module 11 — Bounded delegation and hybrid orchestration
concepts.summary: When a parent agent delegates work, the child must know exactly what was authorized. A signed envelope proves integrity and scope: changing the owner, project, run IDs, claims, evidence, budget, timestamp, nonce, schema, or key version invalidates the signature. HMAC authenticates data under a shared secret. It does not encrypt the content and is not a remote PKI.
concepts.mental_model: Use a sealed review packet. The parent supplies exact claims and evidence IDs; the child cannot fetch more evidence or use tools. The model output is untrusted until strict parsing proves every claim appears exactly once and every cited evidence ID was delegated. The invariant is bounded authority, not model infallibility.
concepts.limitations: The active verifier requires a parent-issued HMAC envelope bound to actual bounded claim/evidence content, owner/project/run scope, budget, freshness, nonce, schema and key version, with durable replay receipts. This authenticates local in-process delegation metadata; it does not encrypt content or establish a remote multi-host PKI.

concepts.title: Learning, optimization, and drift
concepts.module_title: Module 09 — Evaluation harness and regression evidence
concepts.summary: A trustworthy learning loop separates three things: 1. Measurement: compare two versioned evaluation cohorts. 2. Recommendation: describe a bounded prompt, policy, retrieval, or configuration revision. 3. Decision: require a human-bound approval before recording promotion. Cogentrex implements those records and gates. “Promoted” means the recommendation was approved and recorded; it does not mean runtime configuration changed.
concepts.mental_model: A test harness is a ruler. A versioned dataset says what is measured; an evaluator defines marks on the ruler; persistence makes results auditable; a threshold is a policy decision. A precise ruler can consistently measure the wrong thing, so validity must be argued separately from reproducibility.
concepts.limitations: Cogentrex records deterministic descriptive drift warnings and human-approved revision recommendations. Promotion is a durable evidence record only; it does not mutate runtime configuration, train a model, claim statistical significance, or prove live-provider quality. Autonomous unapproved production optimization is deliberately deferred.

concepts.title: Distributed agent networks
concepts.module_title: Module 11 — Bounded delegation and hybrid orchestration
concepts.summary: A distributed agent network coordinates agents in different processes or machines through durable messages and explicit ownership. It must handle duplicates, partial failure, version skew, and network partitions. Several serial model calls inside one API request are not a distributed network.
concepts.mental_model: Treat the boundary as a contract with explicit inputs, outputs, state, failure behavior, and evidence. The important question is not whether a similarly named class or file exists, but whether the behavior is wired into a real path and whether a test or observation proves it.
concepts.limitations: No distributed agent network is implemented; Cogentrex intentionally focuses on one bounded local verifier child rather than claiming a swarm, broker, consensus layer, or cross-node orchestration. No broker, discovery, leases, distributed cancellation, deduplication, cross-node auth, or deployment evidence.

concepts.title: High-throughput model serving
concepts.module_title: Module 14 — Local operations: Compose, health, migrations, CI, and recovery
concepts.summary: High-throughput serving maximizes useful requests or tokens per second while controlling latency and memory. Techniques include continuous batching, request admission, KV-cache management, and backpressure. A web API that calls an external model is not itself a high-throughput model server.
concepts.mental_model: Treat the boundary as a contract with explicit inputs, outputs, state, failure behavior, and evidence. The important question is not whether a similarly named class or file exists, but whether the behavior is wired into a real path and whether a test or observation proves it.
concepts.limitations: Cogentrex does not implement or benchmark a model-serving plane with dynamic batching, admission control, autoscaling evidence, or latency/throughput SLOs; API replicas and an HPA manifest do not establish this capability. No serving engine, batching scheduler, queue policy, GPU topology, load test, or measured capacity.

concepts.title: Fine-tuning and vertical adaptation
concepts.module_title: Module 09 — Evaluation harness and regression evidence
concepts.summary: Fine-tuning changes model weights using a curated dataset. Vertical adaptation specializes a system for a domain and may instead use retrieval, tools, rules, or prompts. RAG changes context, not weights. A safe pipeline needs data lineage, privacy review, evaluation, and rollback.
concepts.mental_model: Treat the boundary as a contract with explicit inputs, outputs, state, failure behavior, and evidence. The important question is not whether a similarly named class or file exists, but whether the behavior is wired into a real path and whether a test or observation proves it.
concepts.limitations: No training, fine-tuning, adapter-weight, model-registry, or promotion pipeline exists; current skills, RAG, and prompts are runtime adaptation and must not be called fine-tuning. No dataset consent pipeline, trainer, checkpoints, registry, offline/online gate, or deployment rollback.

concepts.title: Kubernetes and public deployment
concepts.module_title: Module 14 — Local operations: Compose, health, migrations, CI, and recovery
concepts.summary: Kubernetes declares how containers run, scale, receive traffic, and recover. A public deployment also needs real image provenance, TLS/DNS, secret management, migrations, monitoring, and observed rollout behavior. A YAML manifest in Git is an artifact, not evidence that a cluster works.
concepts.mental_model: Treat the boundary as a contract with explicit inputs, outputs, state, failure behavior, and evidence. The important question is not whether a similarly named class or file exists, but whether the behavior is wired into a real path and whether a test or observation proves it.
concepts.limitations: Historical Kubernetes and Helm artifacts describe possible resources but public/cloud/Kubernetes operation is deliberately deferred. No cluster validation, schema/render gate, TLS/DNS, external secret manager, immutable production image, migration job, public URL, SLO, or rollback evidence exists.

concepts.title: Redacted run export and sharing
concepts.module_title: Module 07 — Durable Run Ledger, replay, fork, and compare
concepts.summary: Run export packages prompts, events, tools, evidence, and metrics for another reader. Sharing changes the trust boundary, so stored data that was safe for its owner may still reveal business context or secrets. Export needs an explicit schema, redaction pass, authorization, expiry, and revocation.
concepts.mental_model: Treat the boundary as a contract with explicit inputs, outputs, state, failure behavior, and evidence. The important question is not whether a similarly named class or file exists, but whether the behavior is wired into a real path and whether a test or observation proves it.
concepts.limitations: Immutable disclosure-scanned exports and expiring/revocable grants are bound to an authenticated recipient and closed purpose. No anonymous public link, external delivery, public hosting, legal-compliance, or production deployment claim is made.

concepts.title: Public anonymous run sharing
concepts.module_title: Module 07 — Durable Run Ledger, replay, fork, and compare
concepts.summary: A chat answer alone cannot explain what an agent did. The Run Ledger stores an ordered, owner-scoped trajectory: policy decisions, tool metadata, evidence IDs, token totals, stop reason, lineage, and bounded display metadata. Replay reads stored facts; fork copies safe conversation state at an event boundary; compare places two stored trajectories side by side. None reruns a model or tool.
concepts.mental_model: The ledger is a flight recorder. RunRow is the flight summary; RuntimeEventRow records ordered instrument readings. It deliberately stores hashes, IDs, counts, and decisions rather than prompts, chain-of-thought, tool arguments, or results.
concepts.limitations: Authenticated recipient-bound sharing is implemented, but anonymous Internet disclosure is deliberately excluded. No public capability URL, abuse controls, CDN/cache invalidation, takedown process, public-edge adversarial evidence, or public deployment exists.

concepts.title: Autonomous unapproved production optimization
concepts.module_title: Module 09 — Evaluation harness and regression evidence
concepts.summary: An evaluation turns examples and expectations into repeatable measurements. Cogentrex has a lightweight live-call EvalHarness , heuristic evaluators, and a stronger durable path that evaluates already-completed Run Ledger trajectories against a versioned, hash-verified dataset. The durable path does not call a model, retriever, or tool.
concepts.mental_model: A test harness is a ruler. A versioned dataset says what is measured; an evaluator defines marks on the ruler; persistence makes results auditable; a threshold is a policy decision. A precise ruler can consistently measure the wrong thing, so validity must be argued separately from reproducibility.
concepts.limitations: Drift reports and human-approved promotion records do not mutate runtime configuration. Unattended production changes are deliberately excluded; no authorized optimizer, shadow/canary controller, hard action budget, automatic rollback, kill switch, or production evidence exists.

vocabulary.definition: A concrete class that implements a port (Protocol) by translating between the core application's typed boundary and an external system's specific API or format.
vocabulary.cogentrex: OpenAI, Anthropic, Foundry, and Ollama typed adapters implement the ModelProvider Protocol. SecureToolRegistry implements ToolExecutor. Each adapter translates between Cogentrex typed values and vendor-specific APIs.

vocabulary.definition: Fields present in a JSON object but not declared by its schema. Strict contracts reject them so misspellings and model-invented arguments cannot slip through.
vocabulary.cogentrex: SecureToolRegistry rejects undeclared tool arguments instead of silently ignoring them.

vocabulary.definition: An authenticated encryption mode that provides both confidentiality and integrity. Each encryption uses a fresh random nonce, and additional authenticated data binds the ciphertext to its intended context.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Used by ScopedEncryptedMemoryRepository with a fresh 12-byte nonce from os.urandom per encryption. AAD binds domain label, owner, project, fact ID, and key version.

vocabulary.definition: Software that repeatedly asks a language model what to do, may call tools, observes results, and stops under rules owned by the surrounding program. An agent is more than one model response.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex is a custom typed runtime, not an agent framework. The AgentRuntime class owns the loop, budgets, policy checks, and event emission while the model acts only as an untrusted planner.

vocabulary.definition: Cryptographic authentication of delegation metadata between parent and child agents. The envelope binds claim/evidence content, scope, budget, freshness, nonce, schema, and key version.
vocabulary.cogentrex: backend/app/delegation/envelope.py issues parent-signed HMAC envelopes bound to actual bounded claim/evidence content, owner/project/run scope, budget, freshness, nonce, schema, and key version with durable replay receipts.

vocabulary.definition: An immutable event record emitted by the runtime at a significant transition. It carries an event kind, iteration number, safe data payload, and token usage for observable execution.
vocabulary.cogentrex: AgentEvent is defined in runtime/events.py. The EventSink Protocol receives these events for SSE streaming, run-ledger persistence, structured logging, and observability export.

vocabulary.definition: A string enum classifying each runtime event: RUN_STARTED, ITERATION_STARTED, MODEL_RESPONSE, TOOL_CALL_REQUESTED, POLICY_DECIDED, TOOL_CALL_COMPLETED, APPROVAL_REQUIRED, RUN_STOPPED, and many others. The closed set makes event handling exhaustive.
vocabulary.cogentrex: AgentEventKind is a closed StrEnum in events.py covering model, tool, policy, approval, delegation, reflection, grounding, and lifecycle transitions.

vocabulary.definition: A frozen dataclass returned when a run finishes, containing the final content, stop reason, iteration count, recorded tool calls, accumulated token usage, optional error, and optional structured output.
vocabulary.cogentrex: AgentResult is defined in engine.py. It is the single return value of AgentRuntime.run(), giving callers a complete typed summary of what happened without inspecting the event stream.

vocabulary.definition: The deterministic program that owns the agent loop, state transitions, budgets, policy checks, events, and stopping decisions. It is the authority; the model is only a planner.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Implemented as the AgentRuntime class in engine.py. It injects Protocol-based ports (ModelProvider, ToolExecutor, PolicyEngine, EventSink) and executes an explicit bounded state-machine loop.

vocabulary.definition: A function that constructs and consistently configures the application object, registering middleware, routers, and startup hooks. Callers can inject controlled collaborators for testing.
vocabulary.cogentrex: create_app() in main.py is the application factory. It creates the FastAPI instance, registers the lifespan handler that initializes repositories and application state, mounts middleware and routers.

vocabulary.definition: An application lifecycle is the ordered set of stages from construction and startup through serving requests to controlled shutdown.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex constructs the FastAPI app, runs lifespan startup and preflight work, becomes ready, serves requests, then tears resources down.

vocabulary.definition: Process-owned shared configuration and services stored on the FastAPI application object, not user or conversation memory. Initialized during lifespan and available to all request handlers.
vocabulary.cogentrex: app.state holds the configured provider, DurableApprovalBroker, persistence redactor, log buffer, and telemetry exporter. Routes access these through request.app.state for request-scoped dependency construction.

vocabulary.definition: A human or host decision bound to an exact tool-call identity and argument hash. It is not a blanket trust grant; it is a one-use ticket that permits only the effect whose identity was shown.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Implemented as DurableApprovalBroker with ApprovalRepository in backend/app/security/live_approvals.py and approval_repository.py. Exact binding covers owner/run/call identity, canonical tool name, and argument SHA-256 digest.

vocabulary.definition: A legacy annotation on a tool indicating whether it should require approval. In the current rule-based policy, unmatched tools with a legacy hint produce ASK; the hint is a fallback, not primary policy.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Stored as part of trusted ToolDefinition metadata. When no policy rule matches, a legacy approval hint produces ASK. Superseded by explicit policy rules when present.

vocabulary.definition: A persisted database row recording an approval decision with user_id, conversation_id, run_id, status, reason, and timestamps. It intentionally stores no raw-arguments field.
vocabulary.cogentrex: ApprovalRecord in backend/app/security/approval_repository.py. Terminal states are APPROVED, DENIED, EXPIRED, or CANCELLED. Conditional SQL update ensures only one transition wins from PENDING.

vocabulary.definition: The time-to-live after which a pending approval automatically becomes expired. This bounds human decision latency so the runtime does not wait indefinitely.
vocabulary.cogentrex: ApprovalRepository.reserve inserts the receipt with a positive TTL. expire_due transitions stale pending approvals. The stop reason approval_timeout fires if the deadline passes.

vocabulary.definition: A deterministic hash of the canonicalized tool call arguments used to bind an approval to an exact invocation. If arguments change, the hash changes and the approval no longer matches.
vocabulary.cogentrex: canonical_arguments_hash in security/policy.py produces a stable hash from canonical_arguments_snapshot. This ensures approvals are exact-bound and cannot be reused for different arguments.

vocabulary.definition: A named output produced during a run, such as generated code or a document. Artifacts are persisted with redaction and subject to the same data boundary controls as other stored content.
vocabulary.cogentrex: backend/app/services/artifacts.py manages artifact storage. Artifacts pass through PersistenceRedactor before storage and are subject to security resource tests.

vocabulary.definition: Storing generated artifacts (code, documents, media) with owner scoping, security scanning, and authenticated access controls.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex persists artifacts with owner scoping and security controls; no durable attachment backend or public hosting is claimed.

vocabulary.definition: Python's cooperative concurrency model where async functions yield control at await points while waiting for I/O. It does not automatically make CPU work faster; it enables efficient waiting.
vocabulary.cogentrex: All provider calls, tool executions, approval waits, and event emissions are async. The runtime uses asyncio for cooperative I/O concurrency, guarded by deadlines to prevent indefinite waits.

vocabulary.definition: A delivery strategy that retries to reduce lost work but may deliver the same operation more than once. Receivers therefore need idempotency.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex treats retries and duplicate requests as possible and uses stable identities plus effect-ledger checks to contain them.

vocabulary.definition: A database constraint or conditional write that lets concurrent attempts choose one winner without a check-then-write race.
vocabulary.cogentrex: The effect ledger relies on database-enforced uniqueness rather than process-local memory.

vocabulary.definition: A generated audio recording that narrates key concepts from a source pack, designed for passive learning during commute or exercise.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex source packs declare audio as a target artifact type; generation follows the documented runbook when that publishing workflow is explicitly executed and reviewed.

vocabulary.definition: Security and operational evidence about attempted tool execution, policy decisions, and authorization events. Audit records are persisted evidence, not real-time alerts.
vocabulary.cogentrex: SecureToolRegistry.execute audits tool_executed events. Policy decisions, approval outcomes, and compliance checks produce audit evidence. Recorded events are control-flow evidence, not tamper-proof WORM storage.

vocabulary.definition: Verifying that a request comes from a claimed identity. Authentication determines who you are; authorization determines what you may do. They are separate concerns.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Local scrypt/JWT/API-key authentication in backend/app/security/auth.py. No external IdP, automated signing-key rotation, or production certification. Tested in test_auth_persistence and test_agent_auth.

vocabulary.definition: Verifying that an authenticated identity has permission to access or modify a specific resource. In Cogentrex, data is scoped to owners and projects.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Owner/project-scoped authorization in backend/app/security/auth.py and backend/app/routes/stream.py. Tested paths do not eliminate the need to review every new query and side effect.

vocabulary.definition: The data structure representing a tool call that requires human approval: native tool_call_id, canonical tool_name, arguments_hash, risk classes, and the matched policy rule.
vocabulary.cogentrex: AuthorizationRequest in backend/app/security/approvals.py. AuthorizationOutcome.binds compares call ID, name, and digest exactly. Mismatch causes fail-closed denial.

vocabulary.definition: An agent automatically changing its own production configuration without human approval; requires safety controls, rollback, and kill switches.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Autonomous unapproved optimization is deliberately excluded from Cogentrex; drift reports and promotions do not mutate runtime configuration.

vocabulary.definition: An owner/project-scoped durable task with atomic claim, lease fencing, heartbeat, retry/dead-letter, and cancellation. Execution is at-least-once, not exactly-once.
vocabulary.cogentrex: backend/app/services/task_queue.py and backend/app/workers/jobs.py implement SQL-based durable jobs. Non-idempotent external-effect job kinds are prohibited because in-process coroutines cannot be forcibly killed.

vocabulary.definition: Durable asynchronous task execution with claims, leases, heartbeat, retry, dead-letter, and cancellation, running outside the request path.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex implements durable owner/project-scoped SQL jobs with atomic claims, monotonic lease fencing, heartbeat, retry/dead-letter, and cancellation; at-least-once, not exactly-once.

vocabulary.definition: Creating checksummed copies of data and proving they can be restored to a known state, supporting disaster recovery objectives.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex local checksummed clean restore is verified; scheduling, off-site storage, PITR, and cloud failover are absent.

vocabulary.definition: The runtime evaluates policy for all tool calls in a model response as a batch before executing any of them. This prevents partial execution followed by denial.
vocabulary.cogentrex: AgentRuntime pre-validates the complete call batch against policy before executing any tool. If any call is denied, the entire batch fails and no tools execute in that iteration.

vocabulary.definition: A standardized set of evaluation cases and metrics used to compare agent performance across revisions or configurations.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex local portfolio benchmark uses deterministic mock evidence; it proves control behavior, not model quality or cross-system comparability.

vocabulary.definition: Checking and normalizing values when they cross from an untrusted or loosely typed source into a trusted domain.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex validates HTTP input, provider output, tool arguments, policy metadata, and persisted records at their boundaries.

vocabulary.definition: Dispatching a constrained sub-task to a child agent with explicit budget, scope, and capability limits rather than giving unrestricted access.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex implements one evidence-only no-tools verifier child; no dynamic swarm, generic reflection, or multi-child orchestration exists.

vocabulary.definition: A hard limit on iterations, tool calls, tokens, time, or output size. Budgets bound agent behavior to prevent unbounded resource consumption or runaway loops.
vocabulary.cogentrex: RuntimeBudget in backend/app/runtime/engine.py configures max_iterations, max_tool_calls, max_tokens, and deadline. Constructed via create_chat_runtime in backend/app/runtime/factory.py.

vocabulary.definition: Checking untrusted arguments every time a tool is requested, even when the tool definition itself was previously accepted.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex validates each model-supplied argument object before policy evaluation and execution.

vocabulary.definition: A caller's signal that in-progress work should stop and clean up. In async Python, cancellation propagates as CancelledError through awaited coroutines, but cannot roll back committed external effects.
vocabulary.cogentrex: The runtime catches cancellation from deadline expiry or client disconnect, performs bounded terminal cleanup, and records a terminal stop reason. Detached non-terminal work may still consume resources.

vocabulary.definition: A structured set of criteria that a capability must meet before it is considered implemented, including evidence, tests, and limitation statements.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex maintains CAPABILITY-ACCEPTANCE.yaml defining acceptance gates for each implemented and deferred capability with explicit evidence requirements.

vocabulary.definition: Project-level settings that enable, disable, or pin specific capabilities (tools, MCP servers, skills) before provider schemas are built. Preferences control what reaches a run without making content trustworthy.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Project capability preferences in the skills-project-instructions system. Can enable, disable, or pin MCP and tool capabilities. Applied during effective-context enrichment before model exposure.

vocabulary.definition: A durable safe state of conversation and run data that can be used for replay and fork. Checkpoints restore server-side state; they do not restore filesystem workspace, process, tool, or external side-effect state.
vocabulary.cogentrex: backend/app/memory/checkpoints.py and backend/app/services/run_ledger.py manage checkpoints. Fork copies selected conversation state and lineage metadata from the checkpoint boundary.

vocabulary.definition: A stateful guard that temporarily fails fast after repeated dependency failures, then permits a bounded recovery probe. It prevents cascading failure by short-circuiting known-broken paths.
vocabulary.cogentrex: backend/app/security/circuit_breaker.py. Breaker state is process-local. Used for PII detection service resilience. External-provider recovery was not observed in final evidence.

vocabulary.definition: A reference from a claim in an answer to a specific evidence item; a citation is useful only if that item actually supports the claim.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex citation structure and conservative support scoring do not establish source truth or overall answer relevance; they are a structural baseline.

vocabulary.definition: A class is a reusable blueprint that defines what data its objects hold and what behavior those objects provide.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex defines service and value classes with focused responsibilities; AgentRuntime is a class whose objects execute bounded runs.

vocabulary.definition: Passing a callable that returns the current time as a dependency rather than calling time.monotonic() directly. This makes time-dependent code testable with deterministic fake clocks.
vocabulary.cogentrex: AgentRuntime accepts a Clock callable (defined as Callable[[], float] in engine.py). Tests inject deterministic clocks to verify deadline enforcement without real waiting.

vocabulary.definition: Placing two stored run summaries and trajectories side by side to identify differences. Compare is not causal inference; a difference does not prove why an outcome changed.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Implemented in backend/app/routes/runs.py and backend/app/services/run_ledger.py. Reads safe persisted fields only. Inherits the Run Ledger's field allowlist.

vocabulary.definition: Mandatory deterministic checks that run before supported chat, document, structured-output, and effect boundaries. A local technical baseline, not legal certification or an external red-team program.
vocabulary.cogentrex: backend/app/security/compliance.py runs mandatory compliance before chat, document, structured-output, and effect boundaries. Admin-only guardrail/fuzz tests in backend/app/routes/red_team.py.

vocabulary.definition: Deterministic rules that run before supported boundaries plus admin-only adversarial tests to probe for policy bypasses and harmful outputs.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex mandatory deterministic compliance runs before chat, document, structured-output and effect boundaries; this is a local baseline, not legal certification.

vocabulary.definition: An EventSink implementation that fans out each event to multiple child sinks (SSE, run-ledger persistence, logging, telemetry) so a single emit() call reaches all observers.
vocabulary.cogentrex: CompositeEventSink in observability/runtime_events.py receives events from the runtime and dispatches them to all configured child sinks. This is the standard production event routing.

vocabulary.definition: The single location in the application where concrete dependencies are assembled and injected into components. Outside this root, code depends only on abstractions (Protocols), not concrete implementations.
vocabulary.cogentrex: create_chat_runtime in factory.py is the request-scoped composition root that wires a ModelProvider, SecureToolRegistry, PolicyEngine, ToolAuthorizer, and EventSink into an AgentRuntime. The lifespan is the process-level composition root.

vocabulary.definition: A navigable diagram or document showing how course concepts relate to each other, helping learners find paths through the material.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex maintains a concept-map.md document and mind-map artifacts that visualize relationships between all implemented and deferred concepts.

vocabulary.definition: A database update that succeeds only while the stored row still matches an expected state.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Approval transitions update rows only while status is pending, so competing decisions cannot both win.

vocabulary.definition: Construct is the lifecycle stage where long-lived services and repositories are created and connected after checks succeed.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex lifespan constructs process-scoped dependencies and stores approved service instances on application state before serving requests.

vocabulary.definition: Automatically reducing context size when the assembled window exceeds the configured token allowance, typically by summarizing older messages while keeping recent ones intact.
vocabulary.cogentrex: backend/app/services/auto_compact.py implements auto_compact_context. The fail-closed bound counts every known provider-visible field using one token per UTF-8 byte plus framing. Intentionally conservative, not provider-exact.

vocabulary.definition: A Python object that defines setup and teardown logic for a with block. Async context managers use async with and are essential for resource management in concurrent code.
vocabulary.cogentrex: The lifespan function is an async context manager that sets up and tears down process-level resources. Tool executions and database connections also use context managers for deterministic cleanup.

vocabulary.definition: Tracking the origin and composition of each piece of context supplied to the model: which instructions, skills, project instructions, and conversation messages contributed to the prompt.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Context provenance in runtime/context_provenance.py records metadata-only provenance for initial context. It is currently initial-context rather than per-call provenance.

vocabulary.definition: Everything sent to the model for one invocation: system instructions, tool descriptions, selected durable facts, recent conversation messages, images, and the current user turn. It is temporary and constructed per-request.
vocabulary.cogentrex: build_messages in backend/app/runtime/context.py assembles system prompt, tool guidance, memory context_text, a bounded set of recent conversation messages (currently 20), and current user input. auto_compact_context handles compaction when the window exceeds bounds.

vocabulary.definition: The bounded amount of text (measured in tokens) a model can consider in a single request; exceeding it loses or rejects information.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex fail-closed context bounds cover roles, content, images (22k tokens each), tool definitions, response schema, and provenance; deliberately conservative.

vocabulary.definition: Automatically building, testing, and validating code changes on every commit to catch regressions before they reach production.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex CI records a green revision-scoped run via GitHub Actions and verify.sh; it does not prove deployment or provider quality.

vocabulary.definition: The deterministic code that owns decision-making authority: loop control, budget enforcement, policy checks, event emission, and stopping. The model proposes; the control plane authorizes and executes.
vocabulary.cogentrex: AgentRuntime is the control plane. It never delegates authority to the model. Provider responses are untrusted proposals that pass through typed validation, policy, and approval before any effect.

vocabulary.definition: The durable chat container a user sees: metadata plus ordered user and assistant messages. A conversation can accumulate many turns and runs over time. It is not a run, memory store, or context window.
vocabulary.cogentrex: ConversationRow in backend/app/services/conversations.py stores ID, title, owner, timestamps, and active flag. Message rows store role and redacted content. Lifecycle is create, use, retrieve/search, and delete.

vocabulary.definition: The ordered sequence of stored user and assistant messages in a conversation. History is larger than what fits in any single context window; build_messages selects a bounded subset.
vocabulary.cogentrex: ConversationRepository retrieves a bounded number of recent messages (currently 20) with authenticated user_id. The fixed count is a retrieval bound, not a token guarantee. One large message can consume far more tokens than many small ones.

vocabulary.definition: The stages a conversation passes through from creation to archival, including how messages are persisted, redacted, and scoped to owners.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex conversation rows are redacted persistent history distinct from encrypted fact memory; automatic expiry is absent.

vocabulary.definition: An object returned by calling an async function. It represents suspended computation that can be resumed at each await point. Coroutines run on the event loop and can be cancelled.
vocabulary.cogentrex: AgentRuntime.run, ModelProvider.complete, and ToolExecutor.execute are all coroutines. The runtime manages their lifecycle within deadlines and cancellation boundaries.

vocabulary.definition: An identifier assigned at request entry and copied across request, log, event, and trace boundaries so that all evidence for one operation can be connected during debugging and audit.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Correlation middleware in middleware/correlation.py attaches a unique ID to each incoming request. This ID propagates into structured logs, runtime events, and OpenTelemetry spans.

vocabulary.definition: A measure of the angle between two vectors; closer to 1 means more similar direction. Used to rank candidate chunks by semantic relevance.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex computes cosine similarity in Python over SQL JSON vectors rather than using pgvector for tenant-scoped document retrieval.

vocabulary.definition: Tracking and enforcing spending limits on model calls, token usage, and compute resources at the run and project level.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex atomic run/project reservation and reconciliation are live-proven for chat, RAG and verifier calls; price-book versioning and budget UI are future work.

vocabulary.definition: The point where information changes trust or retention scope. Persistence, logging, export, and provider transmission each represent a distinct data boundary requiring separate controls.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex distinguishes provider transmission (raw prompt), persistence (redacted), logs (redacted), and export (disclosure-scanned) as separate boundary crossings with independent controls.

vocabulary.definition: Versioned database schema changes applied in a defined order to evolve the data model safely across application revisions.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex uses Alembic migrations through revision 20260826_08; rollback and zero-downtime mixed-version operation are unverified.

vocabulary.definition: A Python class whose common value-object methods are generated from declared fields. Frozen or slotted options add constraints but do not automatically deep-freeze nested values.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex uses frozen, slotted dataclasses for many runtime contracts.

vocabulary.definition: A holding area for jobs or messages that have exhausted all retry attempts, allowing later inspection and manual resolution.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex durable jobs include dead-letter handling after retry exhaustion; operators can inspect and resubmit from the dead-letter state.

vocabulary.definition: An absolute monotonic time by which work must finish. Unlike relative timeouts, a deadline shrinks automatically as time passes and is shared across nested operations.
