vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex learning artifacts may include transcripts for generated audio and video content to support accessibility and text-based search.

vocabulary.definition: A permitted change from one state to another, caused by an event or command.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Runtime code validates lifecycle transitions rather than accepting arbitrary status assignments.

vocabulary.definition: An explicit mapping from current state and event to the next state and action. It makes illegal transitions visible.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex documents and tests closed transition sets for run and durable-control lifecycles.

vocabulary.definition: A line between trusted deterministic code and untrusted external input. Everything crossing a trust boundary must be validated, typed, and constrained before use.
vocabulary.cogentrex: The model is an untrusted planner inside a deterministic control plane. Provider output cannot directly execute effects; the runtime snapshots calls, policy evaluates, approval binds, and the registry validates arguments.

vocabulary.definition: The basic category of value a schema expects, such as string, integer, boolean, array, or object.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex supports a deliberately bounded JSON Schema type subset for tool arguments.

vocabulary.definition: An annotation on a variable, parameter, or return value that declares its expected type. Type hints enable static analysis, IDE support, and serve as executable documentation.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Type hints are used extensively in runtime boundaries: Protocol methods, dataclass fields, and function signatures. They make the contract between components explicit and machine-checkable.

vocabulary.definition: A small object identified by its validated values rather than by a mutable identity, often made immutable.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex uses frozen value objects for runtime messages, tool calls, decisions, events, and budget snapshots.

vocabulary.definition: A persistence layer that stores embedding vectors alongside metadata so they can be queried by similarity for retrieval tasks.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex uses a SQL JSON vector store with Python cosine ranking; this is not pgvector or a dedicated vector database and is explicitly scoped to local use.

vocabulary.definition: Fixed, versioned collections of input-output cases used by the evaluation harness to measure agent behavior consistently across revisions.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex ships a versioned two-case grounded-v1 fixture; this is narrow and not representative production-quality coverage.

vocabulary.definition: A generated or recorded video that visually demonstrates concepts, architecture, or code flow for a specific learning objective.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex source packs declare video as a target artifact type; generation follows documented recipes only when the separate publishing workflow is explicitly executed and reviewed.

vocabulary.definition: The Cogentrex subsystem that teaches stable roadmaps, flows, architecture, evidence, and media recipes through generated and curated artifacts.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex Visual Learning Studio manages source packs, curation roadmaps, NotebookLM integration, and provider-neutral artifact generation pipelines.

vocabulary.definition: Yield is the async lifespan boundary that hands control to the web server after startup and resumes during shutdown.
vocabulary.cogentrex: Cogentrex uses FastAPI lifespan yield to separate successful startup construction from later teardown of process-owned resources.

stories.title: A user sends a message
stories.description: Follow one authenticated request from the browser to a durable, inspectable result.

steps.title: Submit message
steps.explanation: The Workbench submits the user message through the loopback gateway.

steps.title: Establish ownership
steps.explanation: Security middleware and JWT validation establish the caller before protected work begins.

steps.title: Create bounded run
steps.explanation: The runtime creates typed state, budgets, stop conditions, and correlation context.

steps.title: Decide next action
steps.explanation: The bounded ReAct loop asks the configured provider for a response or structured tool request.

steps.title: Govern any effect
steps.explanation: Tool arguments are validated and policy decides ALLOW, ASK, or DENY before execution.

steps.title: Execute or pause
steps.explanation: Approval-bound effects pause durably; allowed effects execute with isolation and idempotency controls.

steps.title: Persist evidence
steps.explanation: Events, outputs, effects, stop reasons, and lineage become durable evidence.

steps.title: Stream result
steps.explanation: Ordered runtime events and the final answer are exposed to the authenticated user for inspection.

stories.title: A model requests a tool
stories.description: See how structured model intent becomes a policy-controlled side effect.

steps.title: Produce structured intent
steps.explanation: The provider emits a named tool request with typed arguments rather than executing code directly.

steps.title: Validate arguments
steps.explanation: Unsupported or malformed arguments fail before policy or execution.

steps.title: Classify effect
steps.explanation: Deterministic policy considers tool, arguments, ownership, and effect class.

steps.title: Bind approval
steps.explanation: ASK creates a durable approval tied to the exact run, tool, arguments, and effect.

steps.title: Prevent duplicate effects
steps.explanation: Idempotency and durable effect state prevent accidental duplicate side effects.

steps.title: Execute in boundary
steps.explanation: The approved tool runs inside its declared isolation and permission boundary.

steps.title: Return observable result
steps.explanation: Structured success or error feedback re-enters the bounded runtime and is recorded.

stories.title: Cogentrex answers with grounded knowledge
stories.description: Separate transient context, durable memory, retrieval, and answer verification.

steps.title: Build run context
steps.explanation: Approved immutable project-instruction snapshots and exact skill revisions join scoped messages and memory; hashes, order, and selection reasons enter provenance without raw bodies.

steps.title: Load durable memory
steps.explanation: Owner and project boundaries restrict which persisted memories may influence the run.

steps.title: Prepare knowledge
steps.explanation: Ingested documents are normalized and divided into retrievable units with provenance.

steps.title: Locate candidates
steps.explanation: Embeddings and similarity ranking locate potentially relevant passages; similarity is not proof.

steps.title: Generate from evidence
steps.explanation: The model receives selected evidence and instructions to keep claims conservative.

steps.title: Verify and cite
steps.explanation: Citation presence and faithfulness are evaluated separately from retrieval relevance.

stories.title: A run becomes evidence
stories.description: Follow runtime events into logs, metrics, traces, evaluation, and the user interface.

steps.title: Emit typed events
steps.explanation: State transitions produce structured events with run and correlation identifiers.

steps.title: Persist the timeline
steps.explanation: Durable ordered events support later inspection, replay, fork, and comparison.

steps.title: Produce operational signals
steps.explanation: Logs, counters, latency metrics, and trace spans provide complementary views.

steps.title: Evaluate recorded output
steps.explanation: Recorded-run evaluators produce durable reports without pretending every metric is model judgment.

steps.title: Detect change
steps.explanation: Candidate behavior is measured and any optimization remains bounded and approval-gated.

steps.title: Surface evidence
steps.explanation: The UI shows timelines, summaries, evaluation reports, and explicit limitations.

stories.title: The local stack becomes ready
stories.description: Distinguish process liveness, dependency readiness, and actual application acceptance.

steps.title: Generate protected runtime context
steps.explanation: The wrapper creates protected infrastructure secrets and records exact runtime metadata.

steps.title: Start dependencies
steps.explanation: Durable stores must become healthy before the backend can claim readiness.

steps.title: Apply schema
steps.explanation: Database migrations run before application traffic is accepted.

steps.title: Start application services
steps.explanation: Each service runs with its own health or containment contract.

steps.title: Prove readiness
steps.explanation: Health and readiness checks prove process and dependency state, not model intelligence.

steps.title: Run acceptance
steps.explanation: Auth, chat, persistence, metrics, migrations, and trace export are exercised through the retained stack.

layers.title: Data and evidence

components.responsibility: Persist users, conversations, approvals, runs, evaluations, and jobs.

components.responsibility: Support scoped cache, coordination, and rate-limiting contracts.

components.responsibility: Ingest, chunk, rank, ground, and cite source material.

components.responsibility: Record idempotency, effects, lineage, exports, and disclosure decisions.

components.responsibility: Correlate operational signals without treating one signal as complete evidence.

components.responsibility: Build, migrate, back up, restore, and prove liveness/readiness.
